newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech parliament agrees budget debate extension.
newsitem.headline: Czech parliament agrees budget debate extension.

text.p: The Czech parliament on Wednesday has voted to extend debate on the 1997 draft state budget beyond its normal recess time of 7 PM (1700 GMT).

Under the rules of the parliament, a vote may not be taken in the plenary after 7 PM (1700 GMT), but deputies agreed to suspend the rules so that debate could continue indefinitely and votes might be taken.
The agreement was made ahead of an expected vote on a plan which may force the government to re-work its 1997 draft state budget before submitting it for a first reading.

The opposition Social Democrats proposed the plan which, in part, would require the government to re-cast its draft budget by the end of October with limits on the transfer of funds within the budget totals, once agreed in parliament.

It would also require a rise in payments to municipalities to compensate for changes in the tax code, and would limit the mayors of major cities to determine discressionary spending up to a maximum of 10 percent of state-provided funds.
The CSSD proposal must go to a vote before the budget draft, which was expected to have a first reading on Wednesday, can go to the floor.
